questions.q: What does release automation replace, per this lesson?
options: The need for Apex tests to ever run
'A person remembers to do this' with 'this happens automatically when a defined event occurs' -- a merge, a tag, a schedule
The entire concept of a sandbox
Git version control itself
questions.explain: Release automation turns manual, easy-to-forget human actions (build a Change Set, click deploy, watch status) into automatic responses to a defined trigger event.

questions.q: In GitHub Actions, what feature lets a production deployment job pause and wait for a named person's approval before it runs?
options: A .gitignore file
The --dry-run flag
A commit message template
Environments with required reviewers
questions.explain: GitHub Actions environments can require named reviewers to approve before a job targeting that environment is allowed to proceed -- the mechanism behind a deliberate production release gate.

questions.q: Per this lesson's three-category split, which category does 'deciding whether this release includes a risky Flow change' fall into?
options: Still manual by design -- a human decision made by a release manager or tech lead
Fully automated
Automated with a gate
This decision never happens in a real release process
questions.explain: The human judgment call of whether to ship something now is deliberately left as a manual decision, even in an otherwise heavily automated pipeline.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what tends to happen to release cadence once a team gets release automation right?
options: Releases become rarer and bigger to justify the automation investment
Release automation has no effect on how often a team ships
Teams tend to move toward smaller, more frequent releases, since each one is lower risk and checked identically every time
Teams stop using any kind of version control
questions.explain: Because the same automated checks run identically every time regardless of size, teams often shift toward smaller, more frequent releases rather than big, rare, high-stakes release days.

questions.q: What is this lesson's actual argument for building an automated release pipeline instead of continuing to use manual Change Sets?
options: The automated path's marginal cost per release approaches zero once the pipeline exists, while a manual release's cost scales with how often you release
Change Sets are officially deprecated by Salesforce and can no longer be used
Manual Change Sets are illegal under GDPR
There is no real argument, both approaches cost exactly the same
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly avoids claiming Change Sets are deprecated -- the real argument is about cost scaling: automated releases get cheaper per release as frequency increases, manual ones don't.
